issues.description: PCI-DSS violation: PaymentDetails interface accepts raw credit card data (cardNumber, CVV) as plain strings. This exposes sensitive payment information throughout the application, in logs, error traces, and potentially in database storage. Handling raw card data server-side violates PCI compliance and creates massive liability.
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card data. Use payment gateway tokenization (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree). Replace PaymentDetails with: `interface PaymentDetails { paymentMethodToken: string; amount: number; }` and obtain tokens from client-side payment gateway SDK.

issues.description: Price manipulation vulnerability: The function accepts payment.amount from the client and compares it to the calculated amount. An attacker could modify the payment.amount field in the request to bypass proper pricing, potentially paying less than required or causing inconsistencies in payment processing.
issues.suggestion: Remove 'amount' from PaymentDetails interface entirely. Calculate the amount server-side only: `const amount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier);` and use this value for charging. Never trust client-supplied prices. Change signature to: `processPremiumPayment(userId: string, paymentMethodToken: string, tier: 'premium' | 'enterprise')`

issues.description: Missing authorization check: The function accepts userId as a parameter without validating it matches the authenticated user. An attacker could call this function with any userId and upgrade someone else's account to premium, causing financial loss and account compromise.
issues.suggestion: Add authentication/authorization check at the start of the function: `if (userId !== authenticatedUserId) { throw new Error('Unauthorized: Cannot process payment for another user'); }` or better, derive userId from the authenticated session context rather than accepting it as a parameter.

issues.description: No idempotency protection: Payment processing lacks idempotency keys and transaction locking. An attacker could submit the same payment multiple times in quick succession (race condition), resulting in multiple charges to the same card before the first transaction completes.
issues.suggestion: Add idempotency key: `async function chargeCard(payment: PaymentDetails, amount: number, idempotencyKey: string): Promise<boolean> { const existing = await db.query('SELECT * FROM payments WHERE idempotency_key = $1', [idempotencyKey]); if (existing.length > 0) return true; await db.query('INSERT INTO payments (card_last_four, amount, status, idempotency_key) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)', [lastFour, amount, 'completed', idempotencyKey]); }`

issues.description: Full card number exposed in application memory and potentially in logs/traces. Even slicing the last 4 digits requires accessing the full card number, which should never be in server-side code. This creates exposure risk if error traces, debugging logs, or memory dumps are captured.
issues.suggestion: Use tokenized payment methods exclusively. Payment gateway should return last4 as part of the token metadata: `const paymentMethod = await paymentGateway.getPaymentMethod(token); const lastFour = paymentMethod.card.last4;` Never pass or store full card numbers.

issues.description: Insufficient card validation: The function validates card format but not integrity. It doesn't implement Luhn algorithm checksum validation, allowing fake card numbers with correct length/format to pass validation. Additionally, it doesn't validate that cardNumber contains only digits.
issues.suggestion: Implement Luhn algorithm validation: `function isValidCardNumber(cardNumber: string): boolean { if (!/^\d+$/.test(cardNumber)) return false; let sum = 0; let isEven = false; for (let i = cardNumber.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { let digit = parseInt(cardNumber[i]); if (isEven) { digit *= 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; } sum += digit; isEven = !isEven; } return sum % 10 === 0; }` However, best practice is to not validate cards server-side at all—use payment gateway tokenization.

issues.description: Expiry date validation has an off-by-one error. The code creates a Date object with `new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1)` which defaults to the 1st day of the expiry month. Cards are valid through the end of the expiry month, but this check rejects cards on the last day of their expiry month.
issues.suggestion: Check against the end of the expiry month: `const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0); // Last day of expiry month` or better: `const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month)); // First day of NEXT month if (expiryDateObj <= new Date()) { return false; }`

issues.description: No input validation or sanitization on userId parameter. While the query uses parameterization (which prevents SQL injection), there's no validation that userId is a valid format or belongs to an authenticated user. This allows unauthorized access checks.
issues.suggestion: Validate userId format and authentication: `export async function hasFeatureAccess(userId: string, feature: string, authenticatedUserId: string): Promise<boolean> { if (userId !== authenticatedUserId) { throw new Error('Unauthorized'); } if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string' || userId.length === 0) { throw new Error('Invalid userId'); } // rest of function...`

issues.description: Error details logged to console may expose sensitive information including stack traces, database connection details, SQL errors, or payment processing details. This information can be accessed through log aggregation services or server access, aiding attackers in reconnaissance.
issues.suggestion: Log only safe error details and use structured logging: `catch (error) { const errorMessage = error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unknown error'; logger.error('Payment processing failed', { userId, lastFour, errorMessage }); return false; }` Never log full error objects or stack traces in production for payment-related operations.

issues.description: Inconsistent error handling: Payment failure returns false instead of throwing an error, but validation failures throw errors. This creates inconsistent behavior where callers must handle both return values and exceptions, leading to potential bugs where payment failures are mishandled.
issues.suggestion: Make error handling consistent. Either throw errors for all failures: `if (!paymentSuccessful) { throw new Error('Payment processing failed'); }` or return a discriminated union for all cases: `type PaymentResult = { success: true } | { success: false; error: string }; async function processPremiumPayment(...): Promise<PaymentResult>`

issues.description: JSON.parse called without try/catch or schema validation. If the database contains malformed JSON in the features column (due to data corruption, manual edits, or migration issues), this will throw an uncaught exception and crash the request handler. Additionally, no validation ensures the parsed result is an array.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling and validation: `try { const features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); if (!Array.isArray(features) || !features.every(f => typeof f === 'string')) { throw new Error('Invalid features format'); } return features.includes(feature); } catch (error) { logger.error('Failed to parse subscription features', { userId }); return false; }`

issues.description: JSON.parse called without try/catch or type validation. Malformed JSON in the database will cause an uncaught exception. Additionally, the parsed data is not validated against the expected schema, allowing type mismatches to propagate.
issues.suggestion: Add validation with Zod or similar: `import { z } from 'zod'; const FeaturesSchema = z.array(z.string()); try { const featuresData = JSON.parse(row.features); const features = FeaturesSchema.parse(featuresData); return { userId: row.user_id, tier: row.tier, validUntil: new Date(row.valid_until), features }; } catch (error) { throw new Error('Invalid subscription data format'); }`

issues.description: Error caught as implicit 'any' type without type narrowing. TypeScript's catch clause types errors as 'any' by default, and this code logs the error without checking if it's an Error instance, potentially logging unexpected types or exposing sensitive data structures.
issues.suggestion: Add type narrowing in catch block: `catch (error) { if (error instanceof Error) { logger.error('Payment failed', { message: error.message }); } else { logger.error('Payment failed with unknown error type'); } return false; }`

issues.description: Card number validation checks length but doesn't validate the string contains only digits. This allows non-numeric strings like 'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' (16 characters) to pass validation, which will cause issues in downstream payment processing.
issues.suggestion: Add numeric validation: `if (cardNumber.length !== 16 || !/^\d{16}$/.test(cardNumber)) { return false; }` However, as mentioned earlier, the best practice is to avoid handling raw card numbers entirely.

issues.description: Hardcoded business logic: Tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) are hardcoded in the function. These values vary by jurisdiction and payment processor, making the code fragile and requiring code changes for different regions or payment gateway switches.
issues.suggestion: Move to configuration: `const TAX_RATE = config.get('payment.taxRate', 0.08); const PROCESSING_FEE = config.get('payment.processingFee', 0.029);` or accept as parameters: `function calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier: 'premium' | 'enterprise', taxRate: number = 0.08, processingFee: number = 0.029): number`

issues.description: SELECT * query fetches all columns from subscriptions table unnecessarily. This transfers more data than needed over the network and increases memory usage, especially problematic if the table has additional columns added in the future.
issues.suggestion: Select only required columns: `const query = 'SELECT user_id, tier, valid_until, features FROM subscriptions WHERE user_id = $1';` This makes the query more efficient and explicit about data dependencies.

issues.description: No caching for subscription data. Each feature access check requires a database query. For applications checking multiple features per request or in rapid succession, this creates unnecessary database load and latency.
issues.suggestion: Implement caching: `const cache = new Map<string, { data: Subscription; expiry: number }>(); export async function getUserSubscription(userId: string): Promise<Subscription | null> { const cached = cache.get(userId); if (cached && cached.expiry > Date.now()) { return cached.data; } const result = await fetchFromDb(userId); if (result) { cache.set(userId, { data: result, expiry: Date.now() + 300000 }); // 5 min TTL } return result; }`

issues.description: Error messages are generic and don't provide actionable information. 'Invalid payment details' doesn't tell the caller which field failed validation, making debugging difficult for both developers and legitimate users who may have input errors.
issues.suggestion: Return specific validation errors: `const validationResult = validatePaymentDetails(payment); if (!validationResult.valid) { throw new Error(\`Payment validation failed: \${validationResult.errors.join(', ')}\`); }` and modify validatePaymentDetails to return: `{ valid: boolean; errors: string[] }`

issues.description: Date comparison doesn't account for timezone differences. The comparison 'validUntil < new Date()' uses local server timezone, which may differ from the user's timezone or UTC, potentially causing premature subscription expiration or extended access.
issues.suggestion: Use UTC for all date comparisons: `const now = new Date(); const validUntil = new Date(subscription.valid_until); if (validUntil.getTime() < now.getTime()) { return false; }` or better, store timestamps as UNIX epoch in the database for unambiguous comparisons.

issues.description: Features array is duplicated and hardcoded in the subscription upgrade logic. If feature lists change, they must be updated in this function. The 'free' tier from the Subscription interface is defined but never assigned features.
issues.suggestion: Create a centralized feature configuration: `const TIER_FEATURES: Record<Subscription['tier'], string[]> = { free: ['basic_todos'], premium: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes'], enterprise: ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes', 'api_access', 'team_collaboration'] }; const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];`

issues.description: Magic number '1' for subscription duration (one year) is hardcoded. This makes it difficult to offer flexible subscription periods (monthly, quarterly, etc.) or promotional periods without code changes.
issues.suggestion: Make duration configurable: `function upgradeUserSubscription(userId: string, tier: 'premium' | 'enterprise', durationYears: number = 1): Promise<void> { const validUntil = new Date(); validUntil.setFullYear(validUntil.getFullYear() + durationYears); ... }` or use a duration enum for different subscription types.

issues.description: No error handling for database query in upgradeUserSubscription. If the query fails (database connection lost, constraint violation, etc.), the error will propagate uncaught, potentially leaving the system in an inconsistent state where payment succeeded but subscription wasn't upgraded.
issues.suggestion: Add error handling and consider transaction wrapping: `try { await db.query(query, [userId, tier, validUntil, JSON.stringify(features)]); } catch (error) { logger.error('Failed to upgrade subscription', { userId, tier, error }); throw new Error('Subscription upgrade failed after payment'); }` Ideally, wrap payment and upgrade in a database transaction.

issues.description: Price calculation doesn't round to 2 decimal places for currency. Floating-point arithmetic can produce values like 10.991999999, which could cause issues in payment processing or display. While some payment processors handle this, it's better to be explicit.
issues.suggestion: Round to 2 decimal places: `return Math.round((basePrice + tax + fee) * 100) / 100;` or better, use a currency library like dinero.js: `import Dinero from 'dinero.js'; const amount = Dinero({ amount: Math.round(basePrice * 100), currency: 'USD' });`

codeQuality.summary: This file contains multiple critical security vulnerabilities including PCI-DSS violations (handling raw card data), price manipulation risks, missing authorization checks, and lack of idempotency protection. The code requires a complete rewrite to use proper payment gateway tokenization and implement essential security controls before it can be safely deployed.

testCoverage.summary: Zero test coverage for critical payment processing code. All 6 functions (2 exported, 4 internal) are completely untested, including security-critical card validation, pricing calculations, and payment authorization logic that directly handles money and user subscriptions.

suggestions.description: Apply dependency injection by extracting separate services for payment processing, subscription management, and validation. This violates Single Responsibility Principle - the module mixes payment gateway logic, database access, business rules, and validation.
suggestions.benefits: Testability increases dramatically (each service can be mocked), responsibilities are clear, and the code follows SOLID principles. Database dependency is explicit rather than hidden.

suggestions.description: Extract repeated 'premium' | 'enterprise' union type into a reusable type alias, and create a TierConfig type for tier-related data. Currently the tier union is duplicated 4 times.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplication, ensures type safety across the module, and creates a single source of truth for tier configuration. Using Record with PaidTier ensures exhaustive coverage.

suggestions.description: Extract separate validation functions for card number, CVV, and expiry date. The 28-line function does three distinct validations with deep nesting.
suggestions.benefits: Each validation is independently testable and reusable. Provides specific error messages instead of generic 'Invalid payment details'. Eliminates deep nesting and early returns.

suggestions.description: Move constants (PRICING, TAX_RATE, PROCESSING_FEE) to module level and simplify calculation. Constants scattered inside function reduce reusability and testing.
suggestions.benefits: Constants are configurable at module level for different environments. Returning breakdown allows displaying itemized pricing to users. Using 'as const' provides literal type inference.

suggestions.description: Replace conditional feature assignment with lookup from TIER_CONFIGS constant. Duplicates feature lists and makes adding new tiers error-prone.
suggestions.benefits: Single source of truth for tier features eliminates duplication. Date calculation is extracted for reusability. Adding new tiers requires only updating TIER_CONFIGS.

suggestions.description: Return consistent error types instead of mixing thrown errors with boolean returns. Currently throws for validation but returns false for payment failure, creating inconsistent error handling.
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling pattern throughout. Callers can handle all failures uniformly without try-catch. Provides detailed error messages and optional success data.

suggestions.description: Extract duplicate subscription validity check into reusable function. Both functions check if validUntil < new Date() with identical logic.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates code duplication and database query duplication. hasFeatureAccess reuses getUserSubscription instead of making separate query. Validity check is centralized and testable.

suggestions.description: Return structured result instead of boolean, and use template literals for query. Boolean return loses error context and forces caller to log separately.
suggestions.benefits: Provides transaction ID for tracking and refunds. Error details propagate to caller instead of being lost in console. No side effects (console.error) in utility function. Type-safe error handling.

suggestions.description: Add readonly modifiers to PaymentDetails properties to prevent accidental mutation of sensitive payment data.
suggestions.benefits: Prevents accidental mutation of sensitive payment data. Signals immutability intent to callers. TypeScript enforces readonly at compile time.

suggestions.description: Extract database repository layer to separate data access from business logic. Currently SQL queries are scattered throughout business logic functions, violating separation of concerns.
suggestions.benefits: Database logic is isolated and testable with mocks. Business logic has no SQL knowledge. Can swap database implementations (Postgres, MongoDB, in-memory for tests) by changing repository. Mapping logic is centralized.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts module violates SOLID principles by mixing payment processing, database access, validation, and business logic. High-impact refactorings include extracting separate services (PaymentGateway, SubscriptionService, Repository pattern), creating type-safe tier configurations, and returning structured results instead of mixed boolean/throw patterns.

recommendations.description: URGENT: Replace raw credit card handling with payment gateway tokenization (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree). The code currently violates PCI-DSS compliance by accepting raw card numbers and CVV codes. This creates massive legal and financial liability. Use client-side tokenization and server-side token processing exclusively.

Fix price manipulation vulnerability by removing client-supplied amount parameter. Calculate all prices server-side only and never trust client-provided payment amounts. Add authorization checks to prevent users from upgrading other accounts.

Implement idempotency protection for payment processing using unique idempotency keys. This prevents double-charging users due to race conditions or network retries. Essential for production payment systems.

Add comprehensive test suite for all payment processing functions. Zero test coverage exists for critical financial logic including card validation, pricing calculations, payment charging, and subscription upgrades. This is unacceptable for production deployment.

Fix expiry date validation off-by-one error that rejects cards on the last day of their expiry month. Add proper error handling for JSON.parse operations to prevent crashes from corrupted database data.

Extract separate services using dependency injection: PaymentValidator, PricingService, PaymentGateway, and SubscriptionRepository. Current code violates Single Responsibility Principle by mixing all concerns in one module, making testing and maintenance difficult.

Implement repository pattern to separate database access from business logic. Create type-safe tier configurations as a single source of truth. Return structured results instead of mixing boolean returns with thrown exceptions.

Add caching for subscription data to reduce database load. Optimize queries to select only required columns instead of SELECT *. Consider implementing batch feature checks for users checking multiple features.
